idea-plugin.name: ddot.it
idea-plugin.description:
Authoring support for ddot.it — Knowledge Graph Notation, a minimal text format for typed knowledge graphs. Each line is a triple — subject ..predicate.. object — written with double-dot separators.

  • Syntax highlighting for .ddot files.
  • Smart, slot-aware completion (subject / predicate / object) with auto-popup on continuation lines.
  • Code folding per subject scope
  • Structure view: AsciiDoc section headings (= Title, == Title, …) as a bold tree, with subjects nested underneath.
  • Canonical formatter — Reformat Code (⌘⌥L) makes every triple self-contained (subject ..relation.. object) with balanced spacing.
  • Rename refactoring (Shift+F6) renames an entity across the whole project, in every role and in embedded blocks; case variants are offered, never renamed silently.
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) on any entity, project-wide.
  • Letter-case check: names that differ only in capitalisation get a yellow warning; Alt+Enter unifies the spelling project-wide.
  • Cardinality checking: violations of relation bounds (via domain/range or the vocabulary's cardinality relations) get a yellow warning that links to where the bound is stated.
  • Entity popup: hover a subject, relation or object to see its relations and inverse relations across the project; click an item to jump to where the triple is stated.
  • Live templates: ddot-typed, ddot-link, ddot-property, ddot-continue, ddot-meta.
  • Tools menu: Format Document, To Full Triples (expand continuation lines so every line is self-contained), Export as JSON — emits JSONL events matching the ddot.it event spec next to the source file.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Unreleased

  • Replaced names. A name the project says is replaced (a ..is replaced by.. has type, also via replaces, followed through chains) gets a yellow warning wherever it is used, linking to the statement; Alt+Enter replaces it, here or in the whole file. Lint rule DL024 from the core analysis, so ddot lint reports it too.
  • Sections in the Structure view. AsciiDoc-style section headings (= Title, == Title, …, also the symmetric == Title ==) now form a tree in the Structure tool window and the file structure popup. Section titles render in bold; subjects are listed under the section they appear in. Skipped heading levels are ignored — a heading nests under the nearest preceding heading with fewer =. Headings inside ddot.it/off regions are left out.
  • Subjects are now deduplicated per section instead of per file, so a subject used in two sections appears under both.
  • Entity popup. Hovering a subject, relation or object — in a .ddot file or a ddot block in Markdown/AsciiDoc — shows what the project knowledge graph states about it: rel → obj1, obj2 per relation, and → rel: x, y for the inverse direction (x, rel, entity). Every item links to where the triple is stated; with several places, a chooser lists them. Hovering a relation lists the triples that use it. Alt+Enter on an entity (Show what the project states about …) opens the same popup on demand. Unsaved edits are included.
  • Reformat makes every triple self-contained. Reformat Code and Format Document now also give each continuation line its inherited subject (..p.. o → s ..p.. o) before normalizing spacing. Metadata blocks, ddot.it/off regions, !!block bodies and prose are left alone. To Full Triples now uses the spec parser to find continuation lines.
  • Project-wide rename. Shift+F6 on a subject, relation or object — in a .ddot file, an embedded block, the Structure view, or via Rename… in the entity popup — renames every exact occurrence across .ddot files and ddot blocks in Markdown and AsciiDoc, in every role including metadata keys and values. Prose, ddot.it/off regions, !!block bodies and commands are never touched. Names that differ only in letter case are listed in the dialog (unchecked checkbox) and in their own preview group, and a notification reports what happened to them. Renaming to an existing name warns about the merge. Invalid names are refused. One undo reverts every file. Find Usages (Alt+F7) uses the same search. Specified in feature-rename.adoc.
  • Cardinality checking. Bounds on a relation — rel ..range.. T ,, ..cardinality.. 1 (also doc:range, min cardinality, max cardinality), rel ..min cardinality.. n, rel ..max cardinality.. n, ..has type.. required, ..has type.. single valued — are checked across the project. They apply to every instance of the relation's domain (rel ..domain.. T, also doc:domain, subtypes included) and to every subject using the relation; an instance without any value violates a minimum. Violating lines get a yellow warning, also in embedded blocks; the tooltip links to where the bound is stated, and Alt+Enter offers Go to cardinality statement. Non-numeric bounds are flagged too. What counts is what the project entails under CDS: values stated through an alias, a sub-relation or an inverse (tail ..is part of.. rex), instances of a subtype of the domain; two names of one thing (same as) count once, chains are not followed. Alternative names (lowerBound, hasType, …) count only where a file declares them with has alias or is alias of. The triple index now also stores metadata pairs (index version 6).
  • Relations without a direction. A relation that ends up under both links to and is linked from — for example through an explicit inverse that contradicts its side — gets a yellow warning on every statement that places it.
  • One source of warnings. Every warning now comes from the core library's analysis, which ddot lint also prints, so the editor and the command line agree. This also shows the linter's report-only pitfalls (DL010–DL012: dot runs and separators that make a line silently not a triple), which the editor did not show before.
  • Letter-case check. A subject, relation, object or metadata name that also occurs in the project in different letter case (Project Eagle / project eagle) gets a yellow warning on every spelling; the tooltip links to where the other spellings are used, and Alt+Enter offers Use '…' everywhere, a project-wide rename of all case variants. Alias statements (Foo ..has alias.. foo, ..is alias of..) are exempt.
  • Security: the bundled jackson-databind 3.x is updated from 3.1.4 to 3.2.3, fixing seven advisories (among them GHSA-cxp5-3px4-pw24 and GHSA-wv8q-qhhj-9h54).
  • The triple index now records the line each triple is stated on (index version 5, rebuilt automatically).

0.1.3

  • Connected JSON (CJ) → ddot.it conversion. Right-click a *.cj.json file in the Project view — or use Tools > ddot.it > Convert Connected JSON (CJ) to ddot.it — to generate a sibling .ddot file. The translation is graphinout's canonical CJ-to-ddot.it mapping.
  • *.cj.json files are now recognised as a dedicated CJ JSON file type backed by the bundled JSON language, so they get JSON syntax highlighting, structure and completion.
  • New Tools > ddot.it action To Full Triples: expand continuation lines by repeating the inherited subject so every line becomes a self-contained triple (metadata blocks and ddot.it/off regions are left untouched).
  • The editor now warns on an incomplete triple whose object slot is empty (e.g. s ..p..), which the event export would otherwise drop silently.
  • Added Marketplace plugin icons.

0.1.2

  • AsciiDoc preview: fixed a NoMethodError: undefined method 'context' for #<Array> that aborted rendering for any document containing a description list (term::). The Treeprocessor that rewrites [source,ddot] blocks now skips non-block children when walking the document tree (dlist entries expose their items as [terms, description] arrays rather than AbstractBlock instances).

0.1.1

  • Marketplace compliance: removed all uses of internal Markdown plugin APIs that blocked the 0.1.0 listing.
    • Markdown preview: ```ddot fences are now coloured client-side by a stylesheet and JS injected via the public browserPreviewExtensionProvider extension point, replacing the previous fenceGeneratingProvider (@ApiStatus.Internal) integration. Visual result is identical; the colours no longer track the editor colour scheme dynamically (CSS can't read it), so they're now static defaults tuned for both Light and Darcula.
    • Fence language provider: dropped the getInfoStringForLanguage override (also internal). The default null return covers it; no user-visible flow exercised this hook.

0.1.0

  • AsciiDoc preview support for ddot blocks. New Tools menu action Install AsciiDoc Preview Extension drops a Ruby AsciidoctorJ extension into <project>/.asciidoctor/lib/; [ddot], [ddotit] and [source,ddot|ddot.it|ddotit] blocks then render with the same role coloring as the editor and the Markdown preview, with titles, ids and roles preserved on the block.
  • Rouge lexer for ddot.it shipped alongside the extension — set :source-highlighter: rouge in your .adoc and [source,ddot] blocks dispatch through the standard Asciidoctor highlighter pipeline against the canonical token vocabulary (tokens.md).
  • Cross-implementation golden corpus at ddot.it/test-data/cases/ — every case has expected.body.html, expected.events.jsonl and expected.tokens.json, asserted byte-equal by the Java preview renderer, the JSONL exporter, the Ruby preview renderer (canonical), and the Rouge / TextMate highlighters.
  • Fixes: continuation lines (..pred.. obj) now colour pred as the predicate, not the object (slot-advance bug); installed .rb files are now stamped with the plugin version on the first line so stale installs are easy to spot (head -1 .asciidoctor/lib/ddot-extension.rb).

0.0.9

  • Embed ddot.it inside Markdown fenced code blocks (```ddot, ```ddot.it, ```ddotit) and AsciiDoc listing blocks ([source,ddot], [ddot.it], …). Highlighting, completion, formatting, rename and find-usages all work inside the embedded fragment.
  • Honour ddot.it/off and ddot.it/on: lines inside an off span are dimmed in the editor, collapsible as a fold, hidden from the structure view, and skipped by the Export as JSON action.
  • Markdown preview: ```ddot fences now render with the same role-aware coloring (subject / predicate / object / metadata / command) as the editor, tracking the active color scheme.

0.0.8

  • Minor change in logging.

0.0.7

  • Refactor away from deprecated IntelliJ APIs.
  • Annotator now logs identifying context (file path, element class, range, text snippet) when it fails.

0.0.6 — Initial Marketplace Release

  • Real PSI, formatter, folding, structure view, completion, JSONL export.
  • Rename refactoring: Shift+F6 on an entity renames every occurrence in the file.
  • Auto-popup of continuation predicates after pressing Enter on a complete triple.

action.description: Expand continuation lines by repeating the inherited subject, so every line is a self-contained triple
Convert the selected *.cj.json file to a sibling .ddot file using graphinout's CJ-to-ddot.it mapping
Export the current ddot.it document as JSONL events to a file next to the source
Reinstall ddot-extension.rb, ddot-render.rb and ddot.rb into <contentRoot>/.asciidoctor/lib/. Usually automatic — use this to repair or force the install.
